question: What minimal gauge/source-coordinate invariant boundary vector should a pre-EFT/UV completion supply at a_on in order to resolve the eight normalized fixed-C2 temporal amplitudes identified by C10.65i plus the independent matching scalar C2?
candidate_boundary_vector: S_ur0 = sigma_ur/k^2 at leading regular order
acceptance: derive the density/curvature invariants from Psi_N=psi_pref-HB and delta_N/(1+w)=delta_pref/(1+w)-3HB
derive theta_N=theta_pref+k^2 B from q_N=q_pref+aWB and q=aW theta/k^2; use this to prove R_khrb0 is gauge invariant rather than subtracting a preferred velocity directly from a Newtonian one
show E_gb2, E_urb2 and E_khr2 are invariant relative-entropy gradient coordinates
treat S_ur0 as gauge invariant because the background anisotropic stress vanishes and the linear anisotropic stress perturbation is therefore invariant
reuse the exact C10.65h proof that C2 is invariant between preferred and Newtonian source coordinates

prove the four density-gradient coordinates (A2,E_gb2,E_urb2,E_khr2) form an invertible reparameterization of (D_b2,D_g2,D_ur2,delta_khr2) for any finite 1+w_khr>0 and arbitrary algebraic psi_pref2 dependence on ordinary gradients
count exactly nine UV matching coordinates: eight normalized temporal directions plus C2; do not count overall primordial normalization

define, but do not yet numerically instantiate, a phenomenological regular-control subfamily with E_gb2=E_urb2=E_khr2=R_gb0=R_urb0=R_khrb0=0 and A2,S_ur0,C2 supplied by an explicitly declared external control
next_if_pass: freeze C10.65m read-only numerical control extraction: estimate A2 and S_ur0 from the low-k standard CLASS control and regenerate the gauge-invariant total comoving source C(k) to estimate a historical-control C2, while labeling all three as phenomenological pre-EFT control values rather than completed-U1 predictions
non_claims: not a derivation of the UV boundary vector values
not proof that the phenomenological zero-relative-entropy/zero-relative-velocity subfamily is selected by a microscopic UV completion
